data.name: Friday
data.gender_notes: Friday is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.short_meaning: Day named after the Norse goddess Freyja
data.long_meaning: In Old English, Frīgedæg, derived from Frīge, the name of the Anglo-Saxon goddess of love, fertility, and war. Later, associated with the Roman goddess Venus, the day was named after her. In Christianity, it is the day of the crucifixion of Jesus Christ. The name Friday carries the meaning “Day named after the Norse goddess Freyja” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Friday usually hope their child will grow to embody day named after the norse goddess freyja and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Friday belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Day named after the Norse goddess Freyja.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Friday total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Friday" is historically linked to the Norse and Roman deities, associating love, fertility, and war with the day. In popular culture, it's the day for the release of new music and video games. The term 'TGIF' expresses the relief and excitement many people feel as the end of the week nears.
data.spiritual_significance: In the Christian tradition, Friday holds deep spiritual significance as the day of the crucifixion and death of Jesus Christ. It serves as a reminder of His sacrifice, which plays an essential role in the believer's faith and salvation. For Christians, taking on additional spiritual practices and attending religious services on Fridays has been a long-standing tradition.
